stem: Use the method $S - rS$ to find the value of $S = 1 + 2\times {=r} + 3\times {=r}^2 + \dots + {=n}\times {=r}^{{=n-1}}$ (the sum of {=n} terms).
solution: The terms are (1, 2, 3, ...) times powers of {=r}, so multiply S by the ratio {=r}: ${=r}S = 1\times {=r} + 2\times {=r}^2 + \dots + {=n-1}\times {=r}^{{=n-1}} + {=n}\times {=r}^{{=n}}$.
Subtract: $S - {=r}S = 1 + {=r} + {=r}^2 + \dots + {=r}^{{=n-1}} - {=n}\times {=r}^{{=n}}$ (the sign of the last term changes).
The geometric part has {=n} terms, first term 1 and ratio {=r}: $\frac{{=r}^{{=n}}-1}{{=r}-1} = {=G}$.
notes: Numeric instance of the book's S-rS method, no symbolic n. Answer is exactly integral (S is a sum of integers).
